# Eternal Life Hospice

> Eternal Life Hospice is an independent, Medicare-certified, CDPH-licensed, and ACHC-accredited hospice care provider serving Ventura County and Los Angeles County, California. We provide physician-directed, nurse-coordinated end-of-life care wherever home is — private residences, assisted living facilities, skilled nursing facilities, and residential care homes — with same-day admissions and 24/7 on-call nursing.

## About

- **Founded by:** Aleksandra Dubina, RN, BSN, Founder & CEO — Certified Hospice Administrator with nearly two decades in healthcare and over eleven years in hospice
- **Headquarters:** 4165 E Thousand Oaks Blvd, Suite 325B, Westlake Village, CA 91362
- **Phone (24/7 admissions & on-call):** 805.953.7273
- **Fax:** 805.953.8530
- **Email:** info@eternallifehospice.com
- **Website:** https://eternallifehospice.com

## Credentials & Compliance

- **Medicare-Certified** — covered under Medicare Part A Hospice Benefit
- **CDPH-Licensed** — California Department of Public Health licensed facility
- **ACHC-Accredited** — Accreditation Commission for Health Care (independent third-party accreditation)
- **Medi-Cal accepted** — for eligible California residents
- **Anti-Kickback compliant** — all referral relationships governed by federal compliance standards

## The Eternal Standard — Four Pillars of Care

1. **Clinical Confidence** — physician-directed care plans, RN-coordinated teams, evidence-based symptom management, 24/7 nurse availability
2. **Guided Presence** — proactive family communication, care navigation, social work, chaplaincy, and bereavement support for 13 months after loss
3. **Whole-Person Comfort** — integrative therapies including music therapy, massage, reiki, aromatherapy, sound bath, pet therapy, audiology support, and end-of-life doula companionship
4. **Compliance-Led Care** — Medicare and Medi-Cal certified, ACHC-accredited, CDPH-licensed, documentation accuracy, ethical referral practices

## Core Hospice Services (Covered by Medicare)

- Physician-directed care planning and oversight
- Registered nurse visits (routine, continuous, respite, general inpatient levels of care)
- Certified nursing aide (CNA) services — bathing, grooming, personal care
- Medical social work — family counseling, advance directive support, resource navigation
- Chaplaincy and spiritual care (non-denominational, available to all families)
- Medications related to the terminal diagnosis
- Medical equipment: hospital bed, wheelchair, oxygen, bedside commode, etc.
- Bereavement counseling — up to 13 months post-loss for the family
- Volunteer companionship and respite services
- 24/7 on-call nurse — available every hour of every day

## Integrative & Comfort Therapies (No Additional Cost to Families)

These therapies are provided by Eternal Life Hospice at no additional expense to families. They are not covered by Medicare or Medi-Cal — Eternal Life Hospice absorbs the cost as part of its whole-person care commitment.

- **Music therapy** — live or recorded music at the bedside; reduces anxiety and pain perception
- **Aromatherapy** — evidence-informed essential oil blends for comfort and calm
- **Therapeutic massage** — gentle touch therapy for relaxation and pain relief
- **Reiki** — energy-based relaxation practice for body and spirit
- **Sound bath** — sustained tones from singing bowls and gongs for deep calm
- **Pet therapy** — certified therapy animal visits
- **Audiology support** — hearing device maintenance and support
- **End-of-life doula companionship** — non-medical presence, legacy work, sacred vigil support

## Coverage Area

Serving 2 counties and 135+ communities across Ventura County and Los Angeles County, California.

**Ventura County cities served:** Thousand Oaks, Westlake Village, Camarillo, Oxnard, Ventura, Simi Valley, Moorpark, Newbury Park, Agoura Hills, Calabasas, Malibu, Ojai, Port Hueneme, Santa Paula, Fillmore

**Los Angeles County cities served:** Beverly Hills, Santa Monica, Sherman Oaks, Encino, Tarzana, Woodland Hills, West Hills, Canoga Park, Chatsworth, Northridge, Granada Hills, North Hollywood, Studio City, Toluca Lake, Burbank, Glendale, Pasadena, North Ranch

## Who We Serve

- Adults with any terminal diagnosis — cancer, heart failure, COPD, dementia, Alzheimer's, ALS, kidney failure, liver disease, stroke, and other life-limiting illnesses
- Patients in private homes, assisted living facilities (ALFs), skilled nursing facilities (SNFs), residential care facilities for the elderly (RCFEs)
- Families seeking comfort-focused care after deciding to stop curative treatment
- Patients who meet the Medicare six-month prognosis criteria (if the illness runs its natural course)

## For Referral Partners (Physicians, Social Workers, Discharge Planners)

- **Referral line:** 805.953.7273 (24/7)
- **Referral portal:** https://eternallifehospice.com/refer
- **Admission timeline:** same-day admissions available; nurse at the door within hours of referral
- **Platforms supported:** WellSky, Ensocare, Aidin, AIDA
- **Liaison available:** dedicated referral liaison for facility partners
- **Complex cases accepted** — we do not decline patients other agencies turn away
- **Documentation:** clean, complete documentation provided back to referring physicians and facilities

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: What is hospice care?**
A: Hospice is a Medicare benefit that provides comfort-focused, physician-directed care for people with a terminal diagnosis and a life expectancy of six months or less if the illness runs its natural course. It covers nursing, medications, equipment, social work, chaplaincy, and bereavement — at little to no cost to the patient.

**Q: How do I know when it's time for hospice?**
A: Signs it may be time: a physician has estimated a life expectancy of six months or less; curative treatments are no longer working or have been declined; the focus has shifted to comfort rather than cure; there are frequent hospitalizations; the patient is losing weight or strength despite treatment; or the patient wishes to be at home with family.

**Q: Does Medicare pay for hospice?**
A: Yes. Medicare Part A covers hospice in full for eligible beneficiaries. Most patients pay nothing out of pocket for hospice services. Medi-Cal also covers hospice for eligible California residents.

**Q: Can I choose my own hospice provider?**
A: Yes. Medicare law gives patients the right to choose any Medicare-certified hospice serving their area. You may also change hospice providers at any time with written notice.

**Q: What happens in the first 48 hours of hospice?**
A: A registered nurse visits within 24 hours to assess the patient, establish a care plan, and ensure medications and equipment are in place. Comfort medications are typically delivered to the home on the first day.

**Q: Does hospice mean giving up?**
A: No. Hospice means choosing quality of life, comfort, and time with loved ones over further curative treatment. Studies show some patients live longer under hospice care because pain and symptoms are better managed.

**Q: What is the difference between hospice and palliative care?**
A: Palliative care can be provided alongside curative treatment at any stage of illness. Hospice is a specific Medicare benefit for people who choose comfort over cure when facing a life expectancy of six months or less. Both focus on comfort, but hospice includes a more comprehensive covered benefit.

**Q: How do I compare hospice providers in California?**
A: Verify Medicare certification at Medicare Care Compare (medicare.gov/care-compare); confirm CDPH licensure at the California Health and Human Services facility search; check for independent accreditation (ACHC, CHAP, or Joint Commission); ask about 24/7 nurse access, response times, and integrative therapies. California has documented fraud issues in the hospice industry — independent accreditation and a clean compliance record are critical factors.

**Q: What is The Eternal Standard?**
A: The Eternal Standard is Eternal Life Hospice's core care framework — four pillars: Clinical Confidence, Guided Presence, Whole-Person Comfort, and Compliance-Led Care.

**Q: How much does hospice cost?**
A: For Medicare and Medi-Cal beneficiaries, core hospice services cost nothing out of pocket. Eternal Life Hospice also provides integrative therapies (music, massage, reiki, sound bath, aromatherapy, pet therapy) at no additional expense to families — these are not covered by Medicare but are provided by Eternal Life Hospice at its own cost.

**Q: How do I refer a patient to Eternal Life Hospice?**
A: Call 805.953.7273 (24/7) or submit a referral online at eternallifehospice.com/refer. Same-day admissions are available. A nurse can be at the patient's door within hours of referral.

**Q: Does Eternal Life Hospice serve patients in nursing homes or assisted living?**
A: Yes. Eternal Life Hospice serves patients wherever they call home — including private residences, assisted living facilities, skilled nursing facilities, and residential care homes across Ventura and Los Angeles counties.
